newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudanese president to visit Kenya on Tuesday. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sudanese president to visit Kenya on Tuesday. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir will pay a brief visit to Kenya on Tuesday for his first trip abroad since a rebel offensive began one month ago.
Unlike many of Sudan's neighbours, Kenya is still on speaking terms with Bashir's Islamic-backed regime.
"The visit is at General Bashir's request but he has not given notice of what he would like to discuss," a senior Kenyan official told Reuters in Nairobi.
The Kenyan foreign ministry said Bashir would arrive at 9 a.m. (0600 GMT) and stay for a few hours for talks with President Daniel arap Moi before heading back to Khartoum.
Sudan has relations ranging from bad to bellicose with Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda.

It accuses the last three of direct military involvement in the rebel offensive launched in early January from the south and east by the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and allied opposition forces.

Sudan has overcome such attacks in the past but analysts say this concerted push comes when Khartoum has seldom been more isolated internationally. It is accused by the United States and other Western nations of supporting radical Islamic groups who export their brand of revolution.

Kenya chairs a committee of a regional group, the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGADD), which was set up in 1992 to promote peace in Sudan between the Arabised north and the black African and mainly Christian south.
"The problem is that Sudan has quarrelled with all the other members of the committee, which only leaves Kenya," the Kenyan official said.
"We have left the door open to Sudan because we don't want it (corrects to insert dropped word "it") to turn into a pariah state."
